Consider the matrix $A=\left[\begin{array}{rr} 0.5 \amp 0.6 \\ -0.3 \amp 1.4 \\ \end{array}\right] $.

Find the eigenvalues of $A$ and a basis for their associated eigenspaces.

Suppose that $\xvec_0=\twovec{11}{6}$. Express $\xvec_0$ as a linear combination of eigenvectors of $A$.

Define the vectors $$ \begin{aligned} \xvec_1 \amp {}={} A\xvec_0 \\ \xvec_2 \amp {}={} A\xvec_1 = A^2\xvec_0 \\ \xvec_3 \amp {}={} A\xvec_2 = A^3\xvec_0 \\ \vdots \amp {}={} \vdots \end{aligned} $$ . Write $\xvec_1$, $\xvec_2$, and $\xvec_3$ as a linear combination of eigenvectors of $A$.

What happens to $\xvec_k$ as $k$ grows larger and larger?
